_about: The curated designation dictionary for the private Healthy360 kitchen workbook importer (master plan v2 §4.11).
Every entry here was decided by a human reading the workbook, and nothing in the importer
ever adds to it. There is no fuzzy matcher, no Levenshtein threshold and no 'looks close
enough' rule anywhere in the import path, because the failure mode of an approximate
matcher on this data is not a wrong report — it is a wrong allergen label. 'Sweet Paprika'
and 'Smoked Paprika' are two characters apart from 'Paprika' and from each other; merging
them would be indistinguishable, to any algorithm, from correcting 'Cripsy Spice'.
aliases            A source designation that means an ingredient already named elsewhere.
Only spelling errors, word order, case, singular/plural and the
abbreviations appendix D lists by name. Never a judgement about
whether two foods are 'basically the same'.
tenant_ingredients Designations the platform library does not carry, created as the workbook's
own rows — unverified, because nobody has checked them, and with no
allergen mapping at all, because the workbook records none. The
importer's allergen-review report lists every one of them.
never_merge        Sets that look mergeable and are not. Recorded so that a future
curator can see the decision was made rather than missed.

_about_recipe_links: Which product on the product list is made by which technical sheet. Curated for the same
reason the designations are: 'Caramelised Onion' and 'Caramilsed Onions' are one product and
'Truffle Sauce' and 'Truffle Mayo' may well be two, and no string distance tells them apart.
A link makes the product inherit the recipe's allergen label, so a wrong one is a wrong label.

recipe_links.note: Two draft versions from two sheets that disagree. Neither is published, so the product has no allergen basis from the recipe until a human picks one.

recipe_links_declined.reason: A truffle mayonnaise and a truffle sauce are plausibly two products. The sheet does not say, so the product is imported unlinked.
The sheet is a marination — an intermediate preparation — and the product is the finished item. Linking them would attach an intermediate's cost to a sold product.
Same: the sheet is the preparation stage, and a second sheet ('Escalope Beef Prep') exists for a different meat.
Pesto Mix is an intermediate consumed by Pesto Mayo, not the bottled sauce on the product list. The product name is also misspelled in the source.
One sheet, two products (white and red). Splitting one formulation across two listings would claim a recipe the workbook does not contain.

never_merge.reason: The v6 turnover (376ecf9) removed the platform row 'Coconut milk', which declared tree_nut scoped us_only. Its alias is withdrawn rather than repointed at a surviving coconut row or promoted to a tenant ingredient: a tenant row carries no allergen mapping at all, so promoting it would have dropped a tree-nut declaration a US customer is owed, and the three rows that remain are different foods. A workbook designation of 'coconut milk' now reports unresolved, which is loud, rather than resolving to something that under-declares, which is silent. The fix is a coconut-milk row in the v6 source carrying tree_nut / us_only like its siblings (OQ-054).
Three distinct products at three distinct prices. Smoked paprika in place of sweet changes a dish; an algorithm that merged them would be two edits away from merging 'Peanut Butter' into 'Butter'.
Fresh and powdered are different purchased goods with different prices and different yields. The same holds for onion, ginger and black pepper.
Four mustards at four prices. All four carry the mustard allergen, so merging would not be unsafe — it would simply be untrue, and the costs would stop reconciling with the sheets.

The misspellings merge; the vinegars do not. A sheet that says 'Red Vineagar' means red vinegar, and a sheet that says only 'Vineager' means the generic — guessing a colour for it would be inventing a formulation.
A cut is not the bird. The library's 'Chicken' has no cut, and folding a breast into it would lose the only thing the sheet actually says.
